findings.title: Donation verify accepts any valid Razorpay signature; client razorpay_order_id never compared to donation row's order id; no ownership check
findings.evidence: donations.ts:176-197 — `if (!isDemoPayment) { if (!body.razorpay_order_id || !body.razorpay_payment_id || !body.razorpay_signature) { return reply.code(400)... } const expected = crypto.createHmac('sha256', razorpayKeySecret).update(`${body.razorpay_order_id}|${body.razorpay_payment_id}`).digest('hex'); ... if (!sigOk) { ... return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Invalid payment signature' }); } }` — the HMAC is computed over the CLIENT-SUPPLIED body.razorpay_order_id and compared to the client signature, but body.razorpay_order_id is NEVER compared to donation.razorpay_order_id (the row's stored order id). The donation is looked up ONLY by body.donationId (line 161-167). No check that request.currentUser.id === donation.user_id either. Compare consultation.ts:270 `if (row.user_id !== userId) { return reply.code(403)... }` and consultation.ts:288 `if (razorpay_order_id !== row.razorpay_order_id) { return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Order id mismatch.' }); }` — both guards present in the consultation handler, both ABSENT in the donation handler.
findings.impact: Forged payment confirmation / free donations. An authenticated attacker creates a ₹10,00,000 donation row (create-order), then calls /donations/verify with the victim donationId plus a VALID Razorpay signature for the attacker's OWN small order (e.g. their own ₹101 test order). The signature verifies because it is a genuine Razorpay HMAC over (attacker_order_id|attacker_payment_id) — the verify code never checks that attacker_order_id equals the donation row's razorpay_order_id. The victim donation row flips to status='paid', a real 80G receipt PDF is emailed, and Razorpay only ever captured ₹101 from the attacker. Because there is also no ownership check, any logged-in user can verify ANY other user's donation. Net effect: large tax-deductible receipts minted for ~₹0; revenue fraud + 80G compliance fraud.
findings.repro: 1) Attacker logs in, POST /donations/create-order {gaushalaId:X, amountInr:1000000} -> donationId=D (status created, razorpay_order_id=O_big). 2) Attacker separately creates+pays a tiny real Razorpay order O_small (₹101) and captures razorpay_payment_id=P_small + signature S_small (valid HMAC over O_small|P_small). 3) Attacker POST /donations/verify {donationId:D, razorpay_order_id:O_small, razorpay_payment_id:P_small, razorpay_signature:S_small}. Backend computes expected=HMAC(O_small|P_small)==S_small -> sigOk=true. Never compares O_small to D.razorpay_order_id. UPDATE donations SET status='paid' WHERE id=D. 80G receipt for ₹10,00,000 emailed. Attacker paid ₹101.
findings.suggestedFix: Mirror consultation.ts exactly: (a) load userId=request.currentUser!.id and after fetching the donation row add `if (donation.user_id !== userId) return reply.code(403).send({ error: 'Not authorized for this donation.' });` (b) before signature compare add `if (body.razorpay_order_id !== donation.razorpay_order_id) return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Order id mismatch.' });` (c) reject if donation.status==='paid' (idempotency, see PBO-10).

findings.title: Temple donations silently mis-attributed as gaushala; temple_id never set; receipts name wrong entity
findings.evidence: createOrderSchema (donations.ts:82-89) accepts only `gaushalaId` — no templeId field. INSERT (line 131-139) writes only `gaushala_id`, never `temple_id`: `INSERT INTO donations (id, user_id, gaushala_id, amount_inr, razorpay_order_id, status) VALUES (...)`. DonationForm.tsx:227-232 comment admits the hack: `// Backend expects 'gaushalaId' — we use it as the opaque cause id / for both gaushalas and temples; the backend stores it as a / string in the donations table.` and sends `gaushalaId: causeId` for BOTH kinds. Receipt generation (donations.ts:201-248) always looks up a gaushala profile: `const gaushalaProfile = await prisma.gaushalaProfile.findFirst({ where: { userId: donation.gaushala_id } })` then `gaushalaName: gaushalaProfile?.gaushalaName ?? 'Darshya Gaushala Network'` (line 244) and the email template (line 258) uses the gaushala name. schema.prisma:1166-1176 confirms donations is polymorphic with BOTH gaushalaId (String) and templeId (UUID FK) columns intended: `// Polymorphic donee. Exactly one of (gaushalaId, templeId) is non-null`.
findings.impact: Every temple donation is stored with temple_id=NULL and gaushala_id=<temple cause id>. The 80G receipt PDF names 'Darshya Gaushala Network' (the fallback) instead of the actual temple, because no gaushala_profiles row matches a temple's cause id. Tax receipts misidentify the donee entity — donors claiming 80G for a temple gift get a receipt naming a gaushala, which can invalidate the deduction. Temple portal revenue reports (temple-portal.ts) which filter on donations.temple_id will show zero donations for every temple. Accounting/reconciliation splits donations across the wrong entity.
findings.repro: Open a temple donation page (causeKind='temple'), donate ₹1100. Inspect the donations row: temple_id IS NULL, gaushala_id=<temple cause id>. Open the emailed 80G PDF: donee reads 'Darshya Gaushala Network'. Query temple portal donations: 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `causeKind: z.enum(['temple','gaushala'])` + optional `templeId: z.string().uuid()` to createOrderSchema. When causeKind==='temple', INSERT temple_id (and leave gaushala_id NULL); when gaushala, current behavior. In verify, branch on which id is non-null to load Temple vs GaushalaProfile and render the receipt with the correct entity name + the temple's own 80G/PAN (add temple tax fields). Update DonationForm to send causeKind + the correct id field.

findings.title: Booking wizard charges only base puja price; ₹51 platform + ₹150 prasad fees shown are never collected
findings.evidence: page.tsx:115-116 `const PLATFORM_FEE = 51; const PRASAD_DELIVERY_FEE = 150;`. page.tsx:424-428 `const totalPrice = useMemo(() => { let total = basePrice + PLATFORM_FEE; if (wantsPrasad) total += PRASAD_DELIVERY_FEE; return total; }, [basePrice, wantsPrasad]);` — this is what is DISPLAYED. page.tsx:575-596 the create-order POST body sends `pujaSlug, templeOfferingId, scheduledDate, scheduledTime, devotees, sankalp, specialInstructions, prasadDelivery, deliveryAddress` — NO amount field at all. page.tsx:615 `amount = data.amount;` and page.tsx:627 `amount,` (Razorpay checkout opens with server-returned amount). Server side booking.service.ts:181-184 `const basePrice = offering.priceOverride ?? offering.pujaType.basePrice; const priceAmount = user.isNri ? offering.pujaType.nriPrice : basePrice;` — priceAmount is base price only, no fees. booking.service.ts:235 `priceAmount,` persisted. payment.service.ts:352 `const amountInPaise = Math.round(Number(booking.priceAmount) * 100);` — Razorpay order created for base price only. Button label page.tsx:1961 `Pay ₹{totalPrice.toLocaleString('en-IN')} with Razorpay` shows the fee-inclusive total while Razorpay charges only base.
findings.impact: Revenue leakage of ₹51 per booking (+ ₹150 for every prasad booking) — the fees are advertised and consented to but never captured. For a ₹751 Satyanarayan Katha with prasad the user is shown ₹952 but Razorpay only charges ₹751; ₹201 lost per booking, scaled across all bookings. Also a display/charge mismatch: the pay button says ₹X but the Razorpay modal opens at ₹X-201, which erodes user trust and can cause abandonment. The tax invoice (pdf-invoice via payment.service.ts:35 amountInr=priceAmount) also shows the lower base amount, so the donor's receipt does not match the price they thought they agreed to. prasadDeliveryRequested is stored but the ₹150 prasad fee is never added to priceAmount anywhere server-side.
findings.repro: Book any puja with prasad delivery on the wizard. Summary card shows ₹{base+51+150}. Click 'Pay ₹{total}'. Razorpay modal opens showing only ₹{base}. Complete payment. DB puja_booking.priceAmount = base; no fee ledger entry exists. Invoice PDF amount = base.
findings.suggestedFix: Decide whether fees are real. If yes: in booking.service.ts createBooking add `priceAmount = basePrice + PLATFORM_FEE + (prasadDeliveryRequested ? PRASAD_DELIVERY_FEE : 0)` (and split platformCommission/priestPayout on the total or only the base per business rule — currently commission is 30% of priceAmount, so fees would also inflate priest payout 70%; likely fees should be platform-kept, so compute commission on basePrice and add fees as a separate non-commissioned line). Persist fee breakdown columns. If fees are NOT real, remove PLATFORM_FEE/PRASAD_DELIVERY_FEE from the display total so the button and modal match.

findings.title: PATCH /bookings/:id has no ownership/role check; any authenticated user can drive any booking through the full state machine and inject arbitrary fields
findings.evidence: bookings.ts:226-260 `server.patch('/:id', { preHandler: [authenticateUser] }, async (request, reply) => { const { id } = paramsWithId.parse(request.params); const body = updateBookingStatusSchema.parse(request.body); const updated = await bookingService.updateBookingStatus(id, body.status, body.data); return { booking: updated }; })` — request.currentUser is never read, no requireRole, userId never passed to the service. updateBookingStatus (booking.service.ts:261-298) signature is `(bookingId, newStatus, data?)` — no userId param, no ownership check, no role check; it only validates the state transition then `prisma.pujaBooking.update({ where: { id: bookingId }, data: { status: newStatus, ...data } })`. The route schema (bookings.ts:43-57) allows `data: z.record(z.any()).optional()` — arbitrary JSON merged into the update.
findings.impact: Privilege escalation + data tampering on every booking. Any logged-in devotee can: (a) confirm their own unpaid booking without paying (PATCH status pending_payment->confirmed), bypassing payment entirely; (b) cancel/advance/complete any OTHER user's booking by id (transition it to cancelled, in_progress, completed, video_uploaded, delivered, or refunded) — the state machine in VALID_TRANSITIONS is the only gate; (c) inject arbitrary fields via `data` (e.g. {priestId: <attacker priest>, priceAmount: 0, platformCommission: 0, priestPayout: 999999, cancellationReason: '...'}) because `...data` is spread into the Prisma update with no allowlist. Confirming without payment + writing a fake Commission row (service:304-323 runs on confirm) lets a user get a 'confirmed' booking + trigger priest assignment + invoice email for free. Setting priestPayout/priceAmount lets attackers manipulate payout accounting.
findings.repro: 1) Attacker logs in, POST /bookings/book to create booking B (status pending_payment). 2) Attacker PATCH /bookings/B {status:'confirmed', data:{priestId:'<attacker-priest-uuid>', priceAmount:0}}. 200 OK, booking.confirmed, no payment ever made, Commission row written, invoice emailed. 3) For any other user's booking C (id guessable/leaked), PATCH /bookings/C {status:'cancelled'} or {status:'refunded'} — succeeds, only the state-machine guard applies.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass userId + role into updateBookingStatus and enforce: only the booking owner may set cancelled (and only via cancelBooking which already has ownership+24h logic); only admin or the assigned priest may drive priest_assigned/in_progress/completed/video_uploaded/delivered; refunded is admin-only (processRefund already requires requireRole('admin')). Replace `data: z.record(z.any())` with a strict allowlisted object schema (e.g. only videoProofUrl/scheduledTimeSlot under specific transitions). Never spread unvalidated data into prisma.update.

findings.title: Home-puja + marriage booking pages are dead-end forms with fake/zero submit — no backend, no payment
findings.evidence:
home-puja/book/page.tsx:110-116 `const handlePay = () => { setPaying(true); setTimeout(() => { setPaying(false); setPaid(true); }, 1800); };` — a pure setTimeout, no fetch, no Razorpay, no /bookings call. page.tsx:118-129 on paid it renders `

Booking confirmed!

` with `Booking ID: BS-20260421-{Math.floor(10000 + Math.random() * 90000)}` — a FAKE randomly-generated booking id. grep of the whole file shows ZERO occurrences of fetch|submit|razorpay|/api/. marriage/book/page.tsx grep for `fetch|submit|payment|razorpay|create-order|confirm|onSubmit|handleSubmit|/api/` returns NOTHING — step 5 (line 613-620) only renders a 'Back to edit' button, there is no pay/submit button at all, so the wizard can never complete.
findings.impact: Two entire booking funnels (home-puja and marriage) are non-functional. Home-puja: user completes the wizard, clicks pay, sees a 'Booking confirmed!' screen with a fabricated BS-... id, believes a pandit will arrive — but no booking row, no payment, no priest assignment, no notification exists. They will wait for a call that never comes. Marriage: user fills the whole form and hits a wall at step 5 with only 'Back to edit' — cannot submit at all. Both are customer-trust and conversion catastrophes on revenue-critical entry points; home-puja is worse because it actively lies (fake confirmation + fake booking number).
findings.repro: Home-puja: go to /pujas/home-puja/book, complete steps 1-5, click pay. Observe 'Booking confirmed! BS-20260421-XXXXX'. Open /bookings — empty. DB — no puja_booking row. Marriage: go to /pujas/marriage/book, complete to step 5 — no pay button exists, only 'Back to edit'.
findings.suggestedFix: Wire both pages to the real booking flow: POST /bookings/create-order (or /from-offering for priest-offered home pujas), open Razorpay checkout with the returned orderId/amount, then POST /bookings/verify-payment, then show success using the REAL bookingNumber from the verify response. Remove the fake handlePay setTimeout + random BS- id generation. For marriage, add the pay button + handler (or route the form to POST /weddings/inquiry if it is meant to be a lead, and relabel the success screen accordingly).

findings.title: Self-onboard forms + admin lead 'CONVERTED' only create/update a Lead; no UserRoleAssignment or provider profile — applicants never become the role
findings.file: apps/api/src/routes/leads-self-onboard.ts:122-208; apps/api/src/routes/admin-leads.ts:394-443; apps/api/src/services/onboarding.service.ts:205-239 (the path that DOES create profiles, never called from leads)
findings.evidence: leads-self-onboard.ts:147-171 — the entire self-onboard handler does only `prisma.lead.upsert({ where: { role_email }, update: {...}, create: {...} })` then sends welcome + admin emails. No call to onboardingService, no userRoleAssignment.create, no panditProfile/templeProfile/etc. admin-leads.ts:396-443 PATCH /leads/:id/status — when an admin sets status='CONVERTED' it does `lead.update({ data: { status, notes } })` (line 412-418) and sends an approval email (line 423-428) saying `Your application ... has been approved. Sign in ... to set up your profile and start taking bookings.` — but it NEVER sets convertedUserId, NEVER creates a UserRoleAssignment, NEVER calls onboardingService.upsertProviderProfile / createProviderProfile. Contrast onboarding.ts:252 `const result = await onboardingService.upsertProviderProfile(userId, parsed.data.role, parsed.data.data);` which IS the correct profile-creation path — but it is only reachable from the authenticated /onboarding/provider route, not from lead conversion.
findings.impact: Every self-onboard applicant (temple, priest, astrologer, wellness, gaushala) is permanently stuck as a Lead row. When admin 'approves' them (status=CONVERTED) the system emails them saying they are verified and can take bookings — but they have no role assignment and no provider profile, so the moment they sign in they cannot access any provider dashboard, cannot be listed, cannot receive bookings, and getPriestId()/profile lookups throw 'account not found'. The partnerships funnel is broken end-to-end: the email is false advertising and the supply side of the marketplace never grows from self-onboard. (The only working path is a user who signs up directly and completes the multi-step /onboarding/provider flow themselves.)
findings.repro: 1) Submit /list-temple self-onboard form -> Lead created, no role/profile. 2) Admin PATCH /admin/leads/:id/status {status:'CONVERTED', sendEmail:true} -> lead.status=CONVERTED, approval email sent. 3) Applicant signs in -> has no TEMPLE_MANAGER role, no templeProfile, temple portal inaccessible. 4) Query user_role_assignments for that email's user -> empty.
findings.suggestedFix: In admin-leads.ts PATCH /leads/:id/status, when status==='CONVERTED': resolve-or-create the User (by email), call onboardingService.upsertProviderProfile(user.id, mappedRole, lead.metadata), set lead.convertedUserId=user.id, THEN send the approval email. Map lead roles to RoleType (see PBO-8). Alternatively, have the approval email deep-link the applicant to /onboarding?role=... so they complete the real provider flow themselves.

findings.title: Booking wizard falls back to hardcoded mock puja data + fake slot availability when API unreachable, then submits the mock templeOfferingId
findings.evidence: page.tsx:386-403 `useEffect(() => { async function fetchPuja() { try { const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE_URL}/pujas/types/${slug}`); if (res.ok) { setPuja(data); } else { setPuja(getFallbackPuja(slug)); } } catch { setPuja(getFallbackPuja(slug)); } ... } })` — any non-2xx or network error silently swaps in mock data. getFallbackPuja (122-226) returns temples with fake ids `to-1`,`to-2`,`to-3` and hardcoded slots. page.tsx:446-473 slot fetch: `} catch { // Fallback: generate mock availability const mockSlots = selectedTemple!.availableSlots.map((s) => ({ time: s.time, label: s.label, remaining: Math.floor(Math.random() * 8) + 2, total: 10 })); setSlotAvailability(mockSlots); }` — fake random availability. page.tsx:583 `templeOfferingId: selectedTempleId,` sends whatever temple id is selected — when fallback is active this is `to-1`/`to-2`/`to-3` (not a UUID).
findings.impact: When the puja catalog API is down or slow, the user sees real-looking temples (Kashi Vishwanath, Trimbakeshwar, Siddhivinayak) with real-looking slots and 'remaining' counts that are pure random — none of it real. If they proceed, POST /bookings/create-order sends templeOfferingId='to-1' which fails the Zod uuid() check (createOrderBodySchema.templeOfferingId is z.string().uuid()) -> 400 -> user sees 'Could not create your booking (400)'. So the fallback is a dead-end that manufactures false availability AND a guaranteed failure at submit, but only after the user has invested in filling the whole wizard. The mock catalog also misrepresents which temples offer which puja and at what price (hardcoded ₹1100/₹751/₹1500), so even pre-submit the user is misled. (Note: create-order's uuid validation does prevent a fake booking from actually being created — so this is a UX/trust bug, not a data-integrity bug, hence MEDIUM not HIGH.)
findings.repro: Block api.darshya.online (or set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL to a dead host). Load /pujas/rudrabhishek/book. Page renders with Kashi/Trimbakeshwar/Siddhivinayak temples and 4 random-remaining slots. Select slot, fill devotees, click Pay -> 400 'Could not create your booking (400).'
findings.suggestedFix: Do not silently substitute mock catalog data. On fetch failure show an honest 'Could not load puja details — please retry' state with a retry button (the loading/!puja branch at 886-913 already exists for the null case). Remove getFallbackPuja entirely, or gate it behind NODE_ENV==='development'. Same for slot availability: show 'Slots unavailable — please retry' instead of random numbers.

findings.title: Self-onboard role enum (PRIEST/TEMPLE/GAUSHALA) != OnboardingService RoleType (PANDIT/TEMPLE_MANAGER/GAUSHALA_MANAGER)
findings.evidence: SelfOnboardForm.tsx:7-12 `export type OnboardRole = 'TEMPLE' | 'PRIEST' | 'ASTROLOGER' | 'WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR' | 'GAUSHALA';`. leads-self-onboard.ts:15 `const ROLE_VALUES = ['TEMPLE','PRIEST','ASTROLOGER','WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR','GAUSHALA']`. onboarding.service.ts:6 `type RoleType = 'PANDIT' | 'STORE_OWNER' | 'ASTROLOGER' | 'WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR' | 'GAUSHALA_MANAGER' | 'TEMPLE_MANAGER';`. Mismatches: TEMPLE vs TEMPLE_MANAGER, PRIEST vs PANDIT, GAUSHALA vs GAUSHALA_MANAGER. (ASTROLOGER and WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR match.) admin-lead-conversion.ts:22 uses the lead enum `['TEMPLE','PRIEST','ASTROLOGER','WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR','GAUSHALA']`.
findings.impact: Today the mismatch is latent because leads-self-onboard only writes Lead.role (a free string) and never calls OnboardingService. But it blocks any future admin 'promote lead -> provider' automation: passing lead.role='PRIEST' into upsertProviderProfile(role) hits `ROLE_STEPS[role]` undefined -> 'Invalid role for onboarding: PRIEST' (onboarding.service.ts:48-51) or createProviderProfile's switch falls to default no-op. So the lead enum and the profile-creation enum are incompatible by design, guaranteeing that PBO-6's fix cannot work without an explicit mapping layer. It also means Lead.role values can never be directly reused as UserRoleAssignment.role values.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a single canonical mapping in one place, e.g. `mapLeadRoleToRoleType(role): RoleType` ({TEMPLE:'TEMPLE_MANAGER', PRIEST:'PANDIT', GAUSHALA:'GAUSHALA_MANAGER', ASTROLOGER:'ASTROLOGER', WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR:'WELLNESS_INSTRUCTOR'}) used by both admin lead conversion and any lead->onboarding bridge. Ideally converge the enums (rename lead roles to the *_MANAGER/PANDIT canonical set, or add TEMPLE/PRIEST/GAUSHALA as accepted aliases in OnboardingService).

findings.title: 'Demo: Simulate Successful Payment' button is always visible (no env guard) and shows a confirmed-booking screen with no backend/payment
findings.evidence:
page.tsx:1967-1976 `{/* Demo payment button (for testing) */}
` — rendered unconditionally in every environment (no process.env.NODE_ENV / NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_DEMO guard). handleDemoPayment (863-882): `setPaymentLoading(true); setTimeout(() => { const bkNum = generateBookingNumber(); safeCapture('payment_success', { bookingId: bkNum, amountInr: totalPrice, currency: 'INR' }); setBookingNumber(bkNum); setBookingSuccess(true); setPaymentLoading(false); }, 2000);` — no fetch, no Razorpay, no /bookings call. Sets bookingSuccess=true which renders the full success screen (917-1013) including `Amount Paid ₹{totalPrice}` (970-972) and a real-looking booking number, plus links to /bookings.
findings.impact: Any visitor (including in production) can click 'Demo: Simulate Successful Payment' and receive a full 'Booking Confirmed!' screen with a booking number and 'Amount Paid ₹{total}', believing they have booked a puja — but no booking row, no payment, no priest assignment exists. They then click 'View Booking' -> /bookings shows nothing. This is (a) a free-booking social-engineering vector (users think they booked and will expect a priest), (b) pollutes analytics with fake payment_success events (safeCapture fires), (c) a customer-support burden (users email with a fake BS- number that does not exist), and (d) trivially exploitable confusion since the button is right under the real Pay button. Severity is LOW only because no real booking is created and no money moves — but the trust/support damage is real.
findings.repro: Open /pujas/<any>/book in production. Scroll to payment step. Click 'Demo: Simulate Successful Payment'. After 2s: 'Booking Confirmed!' screen with fake BS- number and 'Amount Paid ₹{total}'. Click 'View Booking' -> empty. Query DB for that BS- number -> not found.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate the button behind `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' && process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SHOW_DEMO_PAY === 'true'`, or delete it entirely. If retained for dev/staging, render a clearly-fake 'DEMO — no booking created' banner and do NOT set bookingSuccess=true / do NOT fire payment_success analytics.

findings.title: [NEW] Donation verify is not idempotent — double-verify mints a second 80G receipt number + second receipt email for one payment
findings.evidence: donations.ts:169-172 fetches the donation but never checks donation.status before proceeding. donations.ts:216 `const receiptNumber = nextReceiptNumber();` generates a NEW receipt number on every call. donations.ts:221-231 `UPDATE donations SET status='paid', paid_at=now(), razorpay_payment_id=$2, receipt_number=$3 WHERE id=$1` runs unconditionally (no `WHERE status='created'`). donations.ts:236-271 generates + emails the 80G PDF on every call. There is no idempotency record (unlike payments.ts:228 which uses checkAndRecord for webhooks).
findings.impact: If the verify endpoint is called twice for the same donation (user double-clicks the Razorpay handler, network retry, or the Razorpay checkout handler re-firing) the donation is marked paid twice, a SECOND distinct receipt_number is generated and overwrites the first on the row, and a SECOND 80G receipt PDF is emailed to the donor. Two 80G receipts for one payment is a tax-compliance problem (donor could file both) and the first receipt number becomes orphaned/unreconcilable. Combined with PBO-1 (no ownership/order-id check), an attacker could also replay-verify a paid donation to churn receipts.
findings.repro: Donate ₹1100, complete Razorpay checkout -> handler calls /donations/verify once (receipt DR-...-A emailed, status=paid). Call /donations/verify again with the same body -> receipt DR-...-B generated, second 80G PDF emailed, row's receipt_number now DR-...-B.
findings.suggestedFix: After fetching the donation, add `if (donation.status === 'paid') return reply.send({ ok:true, donationId:donation.id, receiptNumber:donation.receipt_number, amount:amountInr, status:'paid', duplicate:true });` to short-circuit idempotently. Generate receipt_number only on the first paid transition.

findings.title: [NEW] Donations have no Razorpay webhook backstop — donations rely solely on client-side verify; a closed browser leaves money captured but donation stuck 'created' with no receipt
findings.file: apps/api/src/services/payment.service.ts:703-803 (processWebhookEvent handles only Payment/booking, not donations); apps/api/src/routes/donations.ts (no webhook route); apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts:193-264 (webhook only resolves prisma.payment rows)
findings.evidence: The Razorpay webhook (payments.ts:194 /payment.service.ts processWebhookEvent) on `payment.captured` does `prisma.payment.findFirst({ where: { gatewayOrderId: paymentEntity.order_id }, include: { booking: ... } })` (payment.service.ts:714-719) — it only looks up prisma.Payment rows linked to puja bookings. Donations are written via raw SQL into the `donations` table with NO corresponding prisma.Payment row (donations.ts:131-139), so the webhook can never match a donation and never marks it paid. There is no /donations/webhook route. The only path to mark a donation paid is the client-side Razorpay handler calling POST /donations/verify (DonationForm.tsx:279-293).
findings.impact: If the devotee pays in Razorpay but closes the tab / loses connectivity before the client handler fires, the donation row stays status='created' forever: Razorpay has captured the money, Darshya never marks it paid, no 80G receipt is generated, no email is sent, and the donee entity never sees the donation in its portal. This is silent revenue capture with no fulfillment + no tax receipt — the worst-case donation outcome. There is also no server-side reconciliation cron visible for stuck 'created' donations. (By contrast puja bookings DO have the webhook backstop, so they self-heal.)
findings.repro: Start a donation, complete Razorpay payment, immediately close the browser tab before the handler runs. Donation row: status='created', paid_at=NULL, receipt_number=NULL. Razorpay dashboard: payment captured. No receipt ever emailed.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (a) write a prisma.Payment row for donations (so the existing webhook finds it) and have processWebhookEvent branch to mark the matching donation paid + send receipt, or (b) add a /donations/webhook route that verifies the Razorpay signature, looks up the donation by razorpay_order_id, and runs the same paid+receipt logic. Also add a reconciliation cron that polls Razorpay for orders still 'created' after N minutes and verifies/captures them.

findings.title: [NEW] Razorpay + Stripe webhook confirmation path skips referral reward — referrals are only credited on the client-verify path, which production does not use
findings.file: apps/api/src/services/payment.service.ts:454-460 (verifyPayment calls tryRewardReferralForBooking),731-738 (Razorpay webhook does NOT),1166-1173 (Stripe webhook does NOT)
findings.evidence: verifyPayment (client-verify path) at payment.service.ts:454-460: `if (shouldConfirm) { await writePujaCommissionOnConfirm(payment.booking.id); void sendPujaBookingInvoice(payment.booking.id); void tryRewardReferralForBooking(payment.booking.userId, payment.booking.id); }` — all three side effects. processWebhookEvent Razorpay `payment.captured` (731-738): `if (payment.booking && payment.booking.status === 'pending_payment') { await prisma.pujaBooking.update({ ... data: { status: 'confirmed' } }); await writePujaCommissionOnConfirm(payment.booking.id); void sendPujaBookingInvoice(payment.booking.id); }` — commission + invoice but NO tryRewardReferralForBooking. handleStripeWebhook `payment_intent.succeeded` (1166-1173): same — commission + invoice, NO referral reward.
findings.impact: In production the canonical confirmation path is the Razorpay/Stripe webhook (the client verify is a fallback). Because only the client-verify path credits the ₹100 referral reward (R-Q2-M-011), most confirmed bookings will silently skip the referral credit. Referrers never get their ₹100 wallet credit for referees whose booking confirms via webhook, defeating the entire referral program. The referralClaim stays in 'signed_up'/'qualifying' forever. Revenue impact = referral incentive fraud/under-delivery + user trust loss.
findings.repro: Referrer R shares code; referee U signs up (referralClaim signed_up). U books a puja and pays. Razorpay fires payment.captured webhook -> booking confirmed via processWebhookEvent (line 731). Check R's wallet: no ₹100 credit. Check referralClaim: still 'signed_up'. Repeat via client verify instead of webhook -> credit appears.
findings.suggestedFix: Extract the post-confirm side-effect block (writePujaCommissionOnConfirm + sendPujaBookingInvoice + tryRewardReferralForBooking) into a single helper and call it from all three confirmation paths (verifyPayment, processWebhookEvent payment.captured, handleStripeWebhook payment_intent.succeeded). tryRewardReferralForBooking is already idempotent (findFirst + status check) so calling it from the webhook is safe.

findings.title: [NEW] Puja verifyPayment has no caller-ownership check — any authenticated user with a valid signature can confirm any booking (asymmetric with store-order verify which IS owner-gated)
findings.file: apps/api/src/services/payment.service.ts:396-467 (verifyPayment — no userId param); apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts:69-106 (/verify — never passes userId); apps/api/src/routes/bookings.ts:1118-1150 (/verify-payment — never passes userId); compare payment.service.ts:602-604 (verifyStoreOrderPayment DOES check storeOrder.userId !== userId)
findings.evidence: verifyPayment signature (payment.service.ts:396-400): `async verifyPayment(razorpayOrderId, razorpayPaymentId, razorpaySignature): Promise<VerifyPaymentResult>` — no userId parameter. It verifies the HMAC, finds the Payment by gatewayOrderId, and captures+confirms with no check that the booking belongs to the caller. payments.ts:76-80 `const result = await paymentService.verifyPayment(body.razorpayOrderId, body.razorpayPaymentId, body.razorpaySignature);` — request.currentUser!.id is never passed. bookings.ts:1124-1128 same — never passes userId. Contrast verifyStoreOrderPayment (payment.service.ts:570-604) which takes userId and enforces `if (storeOrder.userId !== userId) throw new Error('You are not authorized to confirm this order.');`.
findings.impact: Asymmetric authorization: store-order payment confirmation requires ownership, but puja-booking payment confirmation does not. Any authenticated user who possesses a valid Razorpay signature + order_id + payment_id for a booking can confirm it via /payments/verify or /bookings/verify-payment without being the booking owner. In practice the signature is bound to the gateway secret so an outsider cannot forge it for someone else's order — but the owner check is defense-in-depth and its absence means: (a) a leaked/partial signature replay can confirm a booking the caller doesn't own; (b) the puja path is inconsistent with the store path, suggesting the guard was simply forgotten; (c) combined with PBO-4 (PATCH /bookings/:id no ownership) the booking surface has systematically missing ownership checks. Also the orderId in the body (bookings.ts:1112 z.string().uuid()) is the booking id but is never validated against the payment's bookingId.
findings.repro: Victim V creates booking B and pays (Razorpay returns a signature to V's browser). Attacker A who somehow obtains V's razorpay_order_id+payment_id+signature (e.g. from a shared device, logged request, or a buggy client that logs the handler response) calls POST /bookings/verify-payment with their own auth token + those fields -> booking B confirmed, A is not the owner, no error.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a userId parameter to verifyPayment and after finding the payment check `if (payment.booking.userId !== userId) throw new Error('You are not authorized to confirm this booking.');` Pass request.currentUser!.id from both /payments/verify and /bookings/verify-payment. Mirror verifyStoreOrderPayment exactly.

findings.title: [NEW] DonationForm collects donor PAN (required ≥ ₹2000) and dedication but they are never persisted — 80G receipt omits donor PAN
findings.evidence: DonationForm.tsx:127 `const [donorPan, setDonorPan] = useState('');` and 128 `const [dedication, setDedication] = useState('');`. validate() (190-196) forces PAN for donations >= ₹2000: `else if (amountNumber >= 2000) { errs.donorPan = 'PAN is required for 80G receipt on donations ≥ ₹2,000'; }`. These are sent ONLY to Razorpay notes (271-277): `notes: { causeId, causeName, causeKind, dedication: dedication.slice(0,200), donorPan: donorPan.toUpperCase() }`. The /donations/verify call body (287-292) sends only `donationId, razorpay_payment_id, razorpay_order_id, razorpay_signature` — no PAN, no dedication. The backend verify schema (donations.ts:91-96) does not accept them. The 80G receipt PDF (donations.ts:236-248 generate80GReceipt) is called with donorName/donorEmail/amountInr/donationDate/receiptNumber/paymentMode/paymentReference/gaushalaName/gaushala80GNumber/gaushalaPan/gaushalaAddress — NO donor PAN field. The donations table schema (schema.prisma:1163-1192) has no pan/dedication column.
findings.impact: Donor PAN — which Indian tax law requires on 80G receipts for donations ≥ ₹2,000 (Rule 18BBAH) — is collected, validated, and then thrown away. The emailed 80G receipt has no donor PAN, so it is non-compliant for the donor's tax filing at the exact threshold where it matters most. Dedication (donor's 'in memory of...' note) is likewise collected and dropped, a UX promise broken. causeKind is dropped too (feeds PBO-2). Razorpay notes are not queryable by Darshya's DB, so the data is effectively lost the moment checkout closes.
findings.repro: Donate ₹2100, fill PAN ABCDE1234F + dedication 'In memory of grandfather'. Verify the 80G PDF: no PAN field, no dedication. Query the donations row: no pan/dedication columns. Check Razorpay dashboard notes: the data is there but not in Darshya's DB.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `donor_pan TEXT, dedication TEXT` columns to the donations table (migration), accept them in /donations/create-order (persisted at create time, before payment) or /donations/verify, and pass donorPan into generate80GReceipt so the PDF carries it. Persist dedication alongside. Read causeKind to drive the temple-vs-gaushala branch (PBO-2).

findings.title: [NEW] Weddings flow has no payment or booking integrity — it is a lead-capture form only (muhurat compute + inquiry insert), despite being presented as a bookable wedding service
findings.file: apps/api/src/routes/weddings.ts:1-115 (only /muhurat + /inquiry, no booking/payment); apps/web/app/pujas/marriage/book/page.tsx (separate dead-end page, see PBO-5)
findings.evidence: weddings.ts exposes exactly two routes: POST /muhurat (line 28, computes muhurats via findWeddingMuhurats) and POST /inquiry (line 42, raw-INSERT into a WeddingInquiry table with status='NEW'). There is no /bookings, no /create-order, no /verify-payment, no Razorpay/Stripe integration, no wedding booking row, no slot/availability, no pricing capture. The inquiry insert (52-88) stores fullName/email/phone/city/weddingDate/package/guests/budget/message and emails a concierge reply saying 'our wedding concierge will contact you within 24 hours'. The web /pujas/marriage/book page (PBO-5) is a separate dead-end wizard that never calls either weddings endpoint.
findings.impact: The weddings product is marketed as a bookable service (the marriage/book wizard shows tiers, pandits, add-ons, a total price and '+ GST') but the backend has no booking or payment capability for weddings — only a contact-form insert. No money can be captured, no wedding can be confirmed, no priest can be assigned. The marriage/book wizard's total amount is decorative. This is a low-severity finding (no money lost, no data corruption) because the flow is honestly a lead funnel at the API layer, but the web wizard's presentation (price, tiers, 'confirm') implies a transaction that does not exist — a trust/conversion risk on a high-ticket surface.
findings.repro: POST /api/v1/weddings/inquiry with a body -> 201, row in WeddingInquiry, concierge email. Try to find a wedding booking/payment endpoint -> none exists. The /pujas/marriage/book wizard (PBO-5) submits nothing at all.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (a) rebrand the web marriage wizard as an inquiry form (remove tier totals / '+ GST' / fake confirm, POST to /weddings/inquiry, show 'we'll call you' success), or (b) if real wedding bookings are intended, build the booking+payment flow on the bookings/paymentService primitives (wedding booking row, create-order, verify-payment). Do not leave the wizard implying a paid booking that the API cannot fulfill.

findings.title: [NEW] Booking wizard create-order POST has no client-side submit-twice guard and no disable-during-flight on the Razorpay open — double-submit can create duplicate bookings + duplicate Razorpay orders
findings.evidence: handlePayment (550-703) sets `setPaymentLoading(true)` at 562 but the pay button (1942-1964) only uses `disabled={paymentLoading}` — there is no separate 'order created' guard, and nothing prevents a second click between setPaymentLoading(true) and rzp.open() if the state update hasn't re-rendered, nor a second invocation if the first create-order is in flight. The create-order call (575-596) creates a real booking row + Razorpay order server-side on every successful call; paymentService.createRazorpayOrder has idempotency only for an EXISTING initiated payment on the SAME bookingId (payment.service.ts:330-349), but two rapid clicks create TWO distinct booking rows (bookingService.createBooking has no per-user-per-slot dedupe beyond the slot-capacity check, which a race can beat). The Razorpay modal.open is fire-and-forget. There is also no guard preventing the user from clicking 'Pay' again after the modal is dismissed via ondismiss (682-684 sets paymentLoading false) — they can re-click and create another order.
findings.impact: A double-click (or dismiss + re-click) on the Pay button fires create-order twice, creating two puja_booking rows (both pending_payment, both with their own Razorpay order) for the same devotee/slot. The slot-capacity check (booking.service.ts:156-169) is a count-then-insert race, so both can pass under concurrency, overbooking a slot beyond maxBookingsPerSlot. The user pays one Razorpay order; the other booking stays pending_payment forever (orphan). Repeated orphan pending bookings pollute /bookings/my and the admin queue. Lower severity because money is not double-charged (the user only completes one Razorpay checkout) but data integrity (slot overbooking + orphan bookings) is real.
findings.repro: Open /pujas/<any>/book, fill the wizard, double-click the Pay button rapidly before the spinner renders. Observe two POST /bookings/create-order in the network tab -> two booking rows created. Or: click Pay, dismiss the Razorpay modal, click Pay again -> second booking row.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a `creatingOrder` ref guard at the top of handlePayment: `if (creatingOrderRef.current) return; creatingOrderRef.current = true;` and reset it only on terminal failure (not on modal dismiss). Disable the pay button on `paymentLoading || orderCreated`. Server-side, add a unique constraint or pre-check (e.g. unique on (userId, templePujaOfferingId, scheduledDate, scheduledTimeSlot) for non-cancelled pending bookings within a short window) to make duplicate creation impossible. Use a transaction or SELECT FOR UPDATE in createBooking before the count check to close the overbooking race.

notes: All 9 prior bugs CONFIRMED against current code (none refuted, none partial).

payment.service.ts Razorpay + Stripe signature verification is correct (timingSafeEqual, raw-body HMAC default-on) on the paths that exist; the gaps are missing ownership checks (PBO-1, PBO-13), missing referral side-effect on webhook (PBO-12), and no donation webhook at all (PBO-11).
Webhook idempotency (checkAndRecord) is present for Razorpay/Stripe webhooks (payments.ts:228,300) — good. Donation verify has none (PBO-10).

Commission split is computed correctly (Decimal arithmetic, 30/70, idempotent findFirst guard) — writePujaCommissionOnConfirm is fine. The commission is 30% of priceAmount, so PBO-3 (fees not charged) also means fees never enter the commission base.

pdf-invoice.ts correctly renders the charged amount (base price); the issue is that the charged amount != displayed total (PBO-3). 80G receipt (pdf-receipt.ts via donations) omits donor PAN (PBO-14) and names the wrong entity for temple donations (PBO-2).
Weddings API is intentionally a lead funnel (no payment) — flagged as LOW because the API is honest about it; the web wizard's presentation is the real problem (PBO-5, PBO-15).

Logged-out donations are correctly blocked: both /donations/create-order and /donations/verify require authenticateUser (donations.ts:104,152); DonationForm.tsx:208-212 redirects unauthenticated users to login. No logged-out donation revenue path exists.
